item.content:encoded: Hey! I'm Zar, I like writing and drawing and stuff. I wanted to write an SCP for a while and have found so many of them interesting and intriguing for so long. item.title: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hey, I'm bubba808. I am a new user on the SCP wiki user that just got accepted today on 11/24/20. I recently got interested in the wiki again and finally pushed myself to apply and be able to interact with the community. It's possible I will change the name of my account in the future, but people can always refer to me as bubba or bubba808 and I will respond.

I am really looking forward to writing articles for this site because of the amazing ideas you can come up with. Whether its science fiction, horror, or a fairy tale there is something unique about writing on this website because it is collaborative and more open. Most of the writings here were just developed out of people's imaginations. Recently, I've been brainstorming up some SCPs and I have a few ideas. Although they are probably not that unique. I'm definitely not the best writer though so I hope to improve my writing during the course of my time here.

So this month's introduction question is what element best represents you. For me it would probably be earth or rock or whatever you want to call it because it is the most consistent and most sturdy element. I like to think I am reliable but that's debatable to say the least.

item.title: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Good evening beautiful people. I'll be using the handle Influrrno (Before you ask, yes, I came up with that because I like fire and ice motifs just a little too much, and yes, my writing will probably reflect that).

I've only recently been exposed to SCP, but I've always been taken in by unconventional writing formats that breed creativity, so I've been reading up on my skips and tales over the past few months and having a good time.

My ideas for writing SCPs and tales are… well, I'm pretty sure they're mostly a complete mess conceptually (let's just say I have an idea relating to a steel cable that puts holes in people but also its own plot), but I consider myself at least competent in technical writing style, so we'll have to see how this goes. I'm extremely excited to get and give productive feedback, as I'm a strong believer in improvement by acknowledging your own shortcomings.

To answer the forum's question, my classical element would definitely be Earth. I'd like to think that's because I'm steadfast, consistent and solid, but I suspect it's more because I just don't like to move much.

Anyway, hopefully I end up contributing something interesting to the site, or failing that, a bit of friendliness. Cheers mates!

item.title: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hey Mikhail Radzinsky, welcome to the SCP wiki! You seem rather soft spoken, but we are glad to have you here and eagerly await your additions to the site! Try not to burn anything while you're here.
As for writing, just make sure you go through the proper greenlighting process on the idea forums first. Remember that there is no rush, and you should take time familiarizing yourself with how Series 6 articles are formatted. We are a rather unique bunch so I'm sure just reading and being a part of the community will be rather fun for you! For my recommendation, you should check out SCP-5005 its one that adds a sense of mystery, and makes you wonder how someone thought this up.

+ Resources
- Hide Resources

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts.

Sandbox

For hashing out concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by the community if you need help refining your concept.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success!

As far as reading is concerened, you might want to check out our Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular, recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community.

Best of luck!

item.title: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hihi my name is flumbles! Ever since I accidentally stumbled on this place in early high school and consequentially had to sleep with a light on for at least 2 weeks I've been a longtime lurker on this place. While the sheer terror from the things I read here has waned, my appreciation for this place hasn't, and I've finally pulled the trigger and made an account.

Ultimately, I'm looking to write and contribute something. I realize that it'll probably be a long long time before I get to finally publishing, but honestly I think I relish that - no doubt I'll learn oodles of good writing advice in the days to come.

I'm also interested in becoming a advisor/topic expert for medical topics (I'm currently a medical student with a BSc in Biomedical Science), but I'm unsure if I'm too new for that for the time being.

Regardless, I'm happy to be here ^_^. Also I like water because I suck at swimming and I feel like waterbending could make that much easier for me.

item.content:encoded:
Hello, all!

I'm Nerdspartan. I've been interested in SCP since the day I first saw Youtube videos of people playing SCP-087, and later SCP:Containment Breach. Recently, I've stumbled upon the SCP narrative channel TheVolgun, which made me come back to the Foundation.

I love the SCP way of depicting horror in an apathetic and scientific fashion, and I wondered if I could write my own SCPs eventually. So do expect me to post something in the idea critique soon! I will also attempt to do a few critiques of other people's work if I feel confident.

My hobbies include nerdy things like playing video games and making video games (with Unity and RPGMaker), and occasionally writing fictions.

If I were an element, I'd probably be earth, because I am of calm, assertive and thoughtful nature, and I like to live my life steadily, with few unforeseen changes.

Thank you for reading and long live the Foundation!

item.title: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello there, name's Ascentimber, and I'm… here now, I guess.

I have heard of the SCP series since… maybe 2012? 2013? But I was only aware of it as an actual community and not just stories in 2016 or so. I guess I have lurked for some time after, but have just recently found the drive to contribute.

Personally, I have no ideas for SCPs as of yet, but I do plan to write on other things. My main interest here is to actually help the Indonesian SCP translation branch, but I will most likely still write something here. I am doing a lot of independent historical research as of the past year or so, so anything I write will probably be based on history.

If there's anything I would like to ask to any staff members that might reply to my introduction message is: 1. What are the current steps on writing SCPs? and, 2. What are the current steps on writing for the Log of Anomalous Items/Extranormal Events/Unexplained Locations?

Answering the random question, it's probably water. Probably because it's the least mismatching one of 'em all.

Anyhow, I would also like to thank the staffs for the acceptance, and a quick one too. It's almost instantaneous, I would say, unlike the two or three day period that the guide says will take.

item.title: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello, my name is ShinxX, nice to meet you all.

I only recently got into SCP’s recently, I had heard of them before and seen some stories, but never really paid much attention to the overall idea or anything. Recently I saw some videos about various SCP’s and just the idea in general that got me more and more interested. I watched videos from The Rubber, thevolgun, etc. I’m now hooked and reading multiple SCP’s every day.

I’ve always had story ideas trapped in my head that I could never put to paper because of my lack of writing skills, plus I’ve never really been around experienced writers. With my joy of drawing, i hope to make my own webcomic I’m the future. A few story ideas I had I believe could work well as SCP’s and I hope to learn and improve my writing here to make great SCP’s and other stories in the future.

The element that represents me most would probably be earth, I’m usually down to earth and tend to be neutral when it comes to many things.

item.title: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hi all! I'm AzureDisplay (Azure is also fine!). I've been lurking on the SCP wiki for a while (since 2015-ish) and have had quite a few ideas for articles of my own in the meantime. I'm generally kind of anxious about the idea of putting work of my own out there so it took me a while, but here we are!

Some of my biggest hobbies are playing video games, animation, and illustration. As far as potential SCPs I would write, I've always been a fan of the articles that hit just the right amount of weird to stick out in your memory but not so much to drift into "lul so randum" territory. Surreality and fridge horror are always top tier when done right.

Overall I'm excited to be here and interact with the community instead of just lurking in the shadows!

item.title: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hey y'all.

My username is EVANCELION (like evangelion, but with a c instead of a g. No, I don't watch the anime), but you're free to call me Jesse (He/Him).

I've always lurked the site, because my friends and I have always loved SCP- probably since I was 12 or 13, so about 7 years- and it's always been a minor bucketlist goal of mine to get at least one canon SCP. I've got my sandbox page made and I'll tackle my ideas one by one over time, but I'm looking forward to meeting all of you and sharing some of my writing. Outside of writing, I thoroughly enjoy drawing in my free time, and I also like playing video games (though I'm sure most people here probably do).
As far as what element I'm closest to, I'd say fire. I'm overly-passionate about my favorite interests and loved ones, but I can get deflated, or doused, rather, pretty easily. Plus, I'm edgy, so, that's definitely also a factor.

Regardless, it's nice to finally be a member of this wiki. I'm looking forward to participating in the community!

Yes, cool name. No, I'm not a girl. But for the sake of keeping this simple, you are allowed to call me dahlia.

item.title: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded: Hello everyone! Please pay no mind to the cursed username; had to get creative making the account. I've been a fan of the SCP universe for some years now, most of my exposure coming from readings but occasionally I'd sit down to read an article or two. As an aspiring writer I figured joining the site would be a good idea not just for honing my skills and getting to know people with similar interests but to also contribute to a community that has inspired me so much throughout the years. I have a bit of a thing for biology, engineering, physics and cosmic horror so a lot of my work involves gnarly creatures, strange machines, interdimensional shenanigans and incomprehensible cosmic entities. I've been whittling away at an idea for several months now, hopefully I'll have enough time during holiday season to whip up a nice draft. I'm very much looking forward to sharing my ideas with you all!

item.title: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded: Hello. My pen name is buried beneath sand. You can call me bbb, sand, or sandy. I've been very interested in scp's for practically my entire life. item.title: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello, I am Sasboss, I am here because I was a fan of the foundation, and then I found The Scarlet King and the old gods. I want to thoroughly research him and the other old gods and eventually, take on the herculean task of tying all of it together in a single cannon. An example of my research would be my work on The Door To Another World. The entity inside was hinted at being the Scarlet king, but I personally didn't believe that. After extensive research, I found a match for another entity that could was a match for the Destroyer of Worlds. LORD GORAN, The Horned Brute, The Breaker of Kingdoms, Wrath's Flame, Bane of Angels, the Scarlet King's Sixth Hand. I descovered him while snooping in the Serpent's hand database, and it referances him being of "Massive size" and conquered 48 realms. Then, "At an unknown time, Lord Goran became imprisoned when attempting to conquer a universe already subjugated by an Archon of Yaldabaoth.1011 This enraged the Archon who battled and defeated Lord Goran after an hour. The Archon brought Goran by the horns to the Scarlet King, and demanded why his lord attempted to violate the Treaty of Thorns and Flesh.
The Scarlet King apologized and explained Goran acted alone. To make amends, he punished Lord Goran by banishing him to an unknown plane of existence of little interest" The serpent's hand does not know where he might be imprisoned, but I think I do. It aslo state that Goran will be imprisoned until "The Scarlet King needs him again" The dorr to another world references a small salt plane and at the middle, a massive entity is contained with chains, all but one broken. The pieces fit. I belive the mystery is solved. Thank you for excepting me into the foundation.
